question: Do A34's losses arise despite withdrawing heterogeneous covariance mass, and does a learned covariance direction add value over its scale-matched full control?
design: Reconstruct the same four saved leave-pair-out covariance fits and original local components, with no optimizer call. Recover strictly-past mixture weights on the same80 training-validation paths. Cache component evidence/density and verify all Q/G/I/M/B forecasts match A34. Use the identity Q-I = log((1-wM)+wM*exp(M-I)); this is exact predictive accounting, not a causal isolation of covariance and weights.
analysis: For each regime, report step9/24 heterogeneous posterior mass for Q and G, fraction of scored steps with worse M density than I, mass on those steps, and M-B paired differences. Report covariance effective dimension and learned high-frequency variance mass by fold. Retain all four blocks. No optimizing masses, selecting models, target outcomes or claiming a unique cause.
next: Use this accounting to freeze a task-level covariance mixture that retains heterogeneous source classes rather than one pooled diagonal. Learn latent covariance classes from source labels only; exclude the entire held seed pair from every fit and calibrator. Keep the original local risk atom and the same full-dictionary control. No regime-label classifier, oracle support, post-hoc mass tuning or new campaign. Validate the source model before conditional sharing or target decision tests.
